## Library imports
```{r}
#| warning: FALSE
library(scales)
library(tidyverse)
```

## Importing raw data
```{r}
#| warning: FALSE
habit_levels <- c("never", "less1", "1~3", "4~8", "gt8")

col_factor <- readr::col_factor
coupon_col_types <- cols(
  # unordered categories (levels inferred from the data)
  destination   = col_factor(),
  passanger     = col_factor(),
  weather       = col_factor(),
  coupon        = col_factor(),
  gender        = col_factor(),
  maritalStatus = col_factor(),
  occupation    = col_factor(),

  # ordered categories (explicit levels)
  time       = col_factor(c("7AM", "10AM", "2PM", "6PM", "10PM"), ordered = TRUE),
  expiration = col_factor(c("2h", "1d"), ordered = TRUE),
  age        = col_factor(c("below21", "21", "26", "31", "36", "41", "46", "50plus"), ordered = TRUE),
  education  = col_factor(c("Some High School", "High School Graduate",
                            "Some college - no degree", "Associates degree",
                            "Bachelors degree", "Graduate degree (Masters or Doctorate)"),
                          ordered = TRUE),
  income     = col_factor(c("Less than $12500", "$12500 - $24999", "$25000 - $37499",
                            "$37500 - $49999", "$50000 - $62499", "$62500 - $74999",
                            "$75000 - $87499", "$87500 - $99999", "$100000 or More"),
                          ordered = TRUE),
  Bar                  = col_factor(habit_levels, ordered = TRUE),
  CoffeeHouse          = col_factor(habit_levels, ordered = TRUE),
  CarryAway            = col_factor(habit_levels, ordered = TRUE),
  RestaurantLessThan20 = col_factor(habit_levels, ordered = TRUE),
  Restaurant20To50     = col_factor(habit_levels, ordered = TRUE),
  
  temperature = col_integer(),
  .default    = col_integer()   # Y, has_children, toCoupon_*, direction_*
)

raw_data <- read_csv("../data/raw/in-vehicle-coupon-recommendation-1.csv",
                     col_types = coupon_col_types)
```

```{r}
dim(raw_data)
```

## Simple Exploration:
We have 12684 observations, and 26 features. From the dataset description document, we are told that the features fall into one of the four following categories:

1. Scenario-Level (same per-scenario across all individuals)
2. Respondent-Level (same per-person across all scenarios)
3. Consumption-Habit
4. Geospatial (Factors)

I would like to put the features into these groups for now:
```{r}
colnames(raw_data)
```

```{r}
scenario_level <- c("destination", "passanger", "weather", "temperature", "time", "coupon", "expiration")
respondent_level <- c("gender", "age", "maritalStatus", "has_children", "education", "occupation", "income")
consumption_habit <- c("Bar", "CoffeeHouse", "CarryAway", "RestaurantLessThan20", "Restaurant20To50")
geospatial_factors <- c("toCoupon_GEQ5min", "toCoupon_GEQ15min", "toCoupon_GEQ25min", "direction_same", "direction_opp")
```

There is a note that all `toCoupon_GEQ5min` are the same in the dataset so we can drop it (since it won't provide any additional value). We can check that quickly:

```{r}
table(raw_data$toCoupon_GEQ5min)
```
Note: We might also want to consider the redundancy of having both `direction_same` and `direction_opp`, as it may be redundant - `direction_same` is always $\neq$ `direction_opp`.

I would like to check the levels of the consumption habits:
```{r}
# Consumption Frequency
for (loc in consumption_habit){
  cat(sprintf("\n%s:", loc))
  print(table(raw_data[[loc]]))
}
```

## Checking the data quality:
```{r}
# Target balance
raw_data |> count(Y) |> mutate(pct = percent(n / sum(n), accuracy = 0.1))

# Duplicates
sum(duplicated(raw_data))

# Missing habit values: how many, and does it relate to acceptance?
raw_data |>
  summarise(across(all_of(consumption_habit), \(x) sum(is.na(x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "habit", values_to = "n_missing")

raw_data |>
  mutate(any_habit_missing = if_any(all_of(consumption_habit), is.na)) |>
  group_by(any_habit_missing) |>
  summarise(n = n(), accept_rate = mean(Y))

# Redundancy check you mention in text
all(raw_data$direction_same + raw_data$direction_opp == 1)
```

```{r}
overall <- mean(raw_data$Y)        # 56.8% baseline acceptance

```


## Visualizations:
We now present some charts that give insights into the survey data.

From our above table, now visually:
```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5
habit_levels <- c("never", "less1", "1~3", "4~8", "gt8")
habit_labels <- c("Never", "Less than 1", "1-3", "4-8", "More than 8")

loc_labels  <- c(Bar = "Bar", CoffeeHouse = "Coffee house", CarryAway = "Take-away",
                 RestaurantLessThan20 = "Restaurant (under $20)",
                 Restaurant20To50 = "Restaurant ($20-50)")
loc_colours <- c("#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#eda100", "#e87ba4")

raw_data |>
  select(all_of(consumption_habit)) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "location", values_to = "response") |>
  mutate(location = factor(location, levels = consumption_habit),
         response = factor(response, levels = habit_levels, labels = habit_labels),
         response = fct_na_value_to_level(response, level = "Missing")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = response, fill = location)) +
  geom_bar(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75,
           colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = loc_colours, labels = loc_labels, name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Most people rarely visit bars, but take-away and cheap restaurants are regular habits",
       subtitle = "How many times per month respondents say they visit each type of place",
       x = "Visits per month", y = "Number of survey rows",
       caption = "Each respondent appears in about 20 rows, so counts reflect rows, not unique people.") +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
```

Q1) Which coupons get accepted?:
```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
raw_data |>
  group_by(coupon) |>
  summarise(rate = mean(Y)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = rate, y = fct_reorder(coupon, rate))) +
  geom_col(fill = blue, width = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = overall, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_text(aes(label = percent(rate, accuracy = 1)),
            hjust = 1.15, colour = "white", fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = overall, y = 5.6, label = "Average: 57%", hjust = -0.1, size = 3.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, 0.85)) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.6, 0.8))) +
  labs(title = str_wrap("Take-away and cheap-restaurant coupons are accepted most; bars least", 55),
       subtitle = "Share of scenarios where the coupon was accepted",
       x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

Q2) Which features influence coupon acceptance?
```{r}
#| fig-height: 9
scenario_vars <- c("coupon", "destination", "passanger", "weather", "time",
                   "expiration", "toCoupon_GEQ15min", "toCoupon_GEQ25min", "direction_same")

raw_data |>
  mutate(across(all_of(scenario_vars), as.character)) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(scenario_vars), names_to = "variable", values_to = "level") |>
  group_by(variable, level) |>
  summarise(diff = mean(Y) - overall, .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(label = paste(variable, "=", level)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = diff, y = fct_reorder(label, diff), fill = diff > 0)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = blue, "FALSE" = red), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = \(x) sprintf("%+.0f", x * 100)) +
  labs(title = "Context matters: weather, distance, coupon type and expiry all shift acceptance",
       subtitle = "Percentage points above (blue) or below (red) the 57% average",
       x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

Q3) Interaction Between Features
```{r}
raw_data |>
  group_by(coupon, time) |>
  summarise(rate = mean(Y), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n >= 30) |>                      # skip tiny cells
  ggplot(aes(time, coupon, fill = rate)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = percent(rate, accuracy = 1), colour = rate > 0.65)) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#cde2fb", high = "#184f95", labels = percent, name = "Accepted") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "white", "FALSE" = "black"), guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "When you offer matters as much as what you offer", x = NULL, y = NULL)
```
Q6) Coupon Acceptance Based on Habits
```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 3.5
raw_data |>
  mutate(matched_habit = case_when(
    coupon == "Bar"                   ~ as.character(Bar),
    coupon == "Coffee House"          ~ as.character(CoffeeHouse),
    coupon == "Carry out & Take away" ~ as.character(CarryAway),
    coupon == "Restaurant(<20)"       ~ as.character(RestaurantLessThan20),
    coupon == "Restaurant(20-50)"     ~ as.character(Restaurant20To50))) |>
  filter(!is.na(matched_habit)) |>
  mutate(matched_habit = factor(matched_habit, levels = c("never", "less1", "1~3", "4~8", "gt8"))) |>
  group_by(coupon, matched_habit) |>
  summarise(rate = mean(Y), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(matched_habit, rate)) +
  geom_col(fill = blue, width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = overall, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  facet_wrap(~ coupon, nrow = 1) +
  labs(title = "People accept coupons for places they already visit",
       x = "How often they visit that type of place (per month)", y = "Accepted")
```

Lastly, we would like to check which options we have for the various combinations from the survey:
```{r}
raw_data |>
  count(destination, time) |>
  complete(destination, time, fill = list(n = 0)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, destination, fill = n)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n)) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f0efec", high = "#6da7ec", guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Not every context was tested together", x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

From this, we note that we only evaluated `Work` at `7am`, `Home` and `10pm` or `6pm`, and `No Urgent Place` was never evaluated at `7am`.

## Takeaways for `02-data_cleaning.qmd`:
- Drop `car` (99% missing) and `toCoupon_GEQ5min` (constant).
- Drop one of `direction_same` / `direction_opp` (always sum to 1).
- Habit NAs (605 rows with at least one): decide drop vs. "Unknown" category; justify using the missingness check above.
- 74 duplicate rows: decide keep/drop (no respondent ID, so they may be legitimate).
- Set ordered factors: habits, `age`, `income`, `education`, `time`, `expiration`; plain factors for the rest.
- Relabel codes: `1d`/`2h`, `less1`/`gt8`, coupon names, `passanger` → `passenger`; standardize column naming.
- Consider ordered distance (<15, 15-25, >25 min) from the nested `GEQ15`/`GEQ25` flags.
- Rare levels (e.g. some `occupation` categories): decide on collapsing later.
- Modeling caveat: no respondent ID (~567 distinct profiles), so split train/test by respondent profile, not by row.
